text: Install, check or remove the Aidus Agentus Scripts-menu folder in a FontLab user folder. Ported from the legacy repository's install.py. The old installer symlinked the whole plugin into FontLab's Scripts folder, replaced whatever was there, and ran uv sync for the brain. Here the host package is installed with uv pip (README), and this module only manages <user folder>/Scripts/Aidus Agentus : the same three thin menu scripts as the repository's Scripts/Aidus Agentus/ folder plus a manifest ( .fontlab-aidus-agentus-install , format 1) holding the sha256 of every file it wrote. Ownership is per file: unknown entries are kept, a modified, foreign or symlinked entry stops an install before anything changes, and uninstall removes only unmodified owned files and the folder only when it is then empty. A folder without a valid manifest, including the workspace orchestrator's symlink, is never touched. Run on the host, not inside FontLab: fontlab-aidus-install {install,check,uninstall} .

text: Aidus Agentus Core — entry point for the AgentPool ACP server. FontLab 9's embedded PythonQt cannot run modern AI libraries, so the AI brain lives in a separate process (here) and communicates with the Plugin over stdin/stdout using JSON-RPC 2.0 (ACP protocol). This module is launched by the Plugin via QProcess::start(). It: 1. Configures structlog (console format when attached to a tty, JSON otherwise) 2. Reads agents.yml, which defines the three LLM agents and their tools 3. Selects native MCP or plugin tools and starts AgentPool's stdio ACP server The server runs until the Plugin closes the QProcess pipe.
title: fontlab_aidus_agentus.core.boot

text: ACP client: manages the JSON-RPC session between the Plugin and the Core. The Plugin (running inside FontLab's PythonQt) uses this client to talk to the Core process over a QProcess stdio pipe. The wire format is newline- delimited JSON (JSON-RPC 2.0). State machine (7 states): DISCONNECTED → INITIALIZING → INITIALIZED → SESSION_PENDING → READY ↕ WAITING ↕ ERROR → DISCONNECTED Signals emitted (connect these in the UI layer): chatUpdate(role, content) — streamed LLM tokens and tool results stateChanged(new_state) — so the UI can show connection status errorOccurred(code, msg) — surfaced to the user as actionable hints All calls into FontLab's sandbox go through the Executor, not through this client. This client only handles the ACP wire protocol.

text: FontLab tool executor: runs LLM-requested operations inside FontLab's sandbox. When the Core's LLM decides to call a tool (e.g. run_fontlab_script ), it sends a tool-call request back over stdin. The Plugin picks this up, routes it here, and executes it inside FontLab's Python environment. The sandbox strips dangerous builtins (eval, exec, import , open) and captures stdout so script output can be returned to the LLM as a tool result. Tools are registered via :class: ToolRegistry . Each tool entry carries: - A handler callable - Metadata: required_params, optional_params, description, requires_font, requires_glyph Outside FontLab (e.g. during static analysis), the fontlab import fails gracefully: FL_AVAILABLE is False and tool calls return an error response rather than crashing.

text: QProcess transport: stdio pipe between the Plugin and the Core process. The Core (fontlab_aidus_agentus.core) runs as a child process launched via QProcess. Messages are newline-delimited JSON written to the child's stdin and read from its stdout. This module owns that pipe. State machine (4 states): DISCONNECTED → CONNECTING → CONNECTED ↕ ERROR → DISCONNECTED Explicit standalone reconnection uses exponential backoff, max 3 attempts. The embedded client owns reconnect/start/initialize/session negotiation; no automatic process restart or replay is performed after a failure. Buffer handling: QProcess delivers data in chunks. The transport accumulates bytes in an internal buffer and only dispatches complete lines (terminated by \n ). Lines exceeding 64 KB are chunked on write to avoid QProcess pipe stalls. All methods must be called from the Qt main thread. Signals are emitted synchronously on the main thread via Qt's event loop.
title: fontlab_aidus_agentus.plugin.transport

text: The FontLab Python API is a C++/Python binding layer: Python Script ↓ fontlab module ↓ C++ model objects fl* classes (flNode, flContour, flShape, flLayer, flGlyph, flPackage…) ↓ fontgate (fg*) fgGlyph, fgFont, fgContour… The class articles document registered names, member kinds, calling conventions and property access. Some APIs depend on build flags. The separate fontgate module and inherited PythonQt/Qt APIs are outside this inventory. CurrentFont() returns fgFont , and CurrentGlyph() returns fgGlyph . Use fl.flPackage(fg_font) or fl.flGlyph(fg_glyph) when calling the model APIs described by the fl* guides. Constructing a wrapper from an existing model object does not imply an independent geometry copy; use the appropriate clone() operation when a separate object is needed.
title: Architecture

text: Throughout the documentation, types use these conventions: Type Meaning str Python string (C++ QString ) float Python float (C++ double ) int Python integer bool Python bool QPointF Qt 2D point; use PythonQt.QtCore.QPointF unless the specific overload documents tuple conversion QRectF Qt rectangle; use PythonQt.QtCore.QRectF unless the specific overload documents tuple conversion QTransform 3×3 matrix — passed as a QTransform -like object QColor Qt color; use PythonQt.QtGui.QColor unless the specific overload documents tuple conversion list(T) Python list of type T T/None Returns T or Python None

text: Python API changes in FontLab 9.1 (build 9812), recorded from the C++ source. The shipped stubs now come from a FontLab 9.1.9813 capture and declare these members ( fgBrush.size is gone). This module records each new or removed name, its signature and its source location, and gives hasattr-based feature detection for hosts that may still run 9.0. It also gives two guarded helpers for the clipboard JSON calls. Status: member presence and the QByteArray route are verified live on FontLab 9.1.9812 (2026-11-16): every NEW_IN_9_1 member exists by hasattr ( flPackage.info members checked on a real font's info ) and fgBrush.size is absent; QtCore.QByteArray(raw) round-trips through getObjectsFromJsonData . Passing a Python bytes object to getObjectsFromJsonData crashes FontLab (SIGBUS in the native QByteArray converter). text: Glyph-level adapter over fontlab_pens.fontgate . Fontport's native model is an fgGlyph whose outline lives on glyph.layer , with glyph-level components. Pens target layers and elements only, so this module resolves the glyph itself: contours are validated, then written by fontlab_pens.fontgate.FontGatePointPen into the layer's first element (point names and smooth flags kept); components stay on glyph.components . Empty native contours are never passed to fgContour.drawPoints, whose implementation dereferences the first node without checking its existence. The target kind is stated to pens ( kind= ), not detected from the native type name, so the same code serves FontGate objects and the duck-typed offline doubles. Only public fontlab_pens names are used.

text: The current Cocoa graphics state over a QPainter (R032). Cocoa draws through an implicit current context with a transform (CTM), a fill and stroke colour, and a save/restore stack. Here that state lives in Python: affine transforms are 6-tuples (m11, m12, m21, m22, tx, ty) composed with plain arithmetic, and a QTransform is built only when a shape is painted (no arithmetic on PythonQt wrappers; unary minus on them crashes FontLab). The base transform maps the drawing space (glyph units, or a view's y-up coordinates) to widget pixels. A context exists only inside a scope ( paint_scope for editor painters, view_scope for NSView.drawRect_ ). State operations outside one raise RuntimeError ; path painting with no destination is a no-op, as in Cocoa. A retained painter cannot paint after its callback.

text: Glyph-editor painters on FontLab's native canvas hooks (resolves R054). Builds with flCanvas.appendPythonPainter(callback, order) call Python inside the canvas paint: UnderOwner before the glyphs are drawn, OverOwner after them. callback(painter, canvas) gets a painter that FontLab has saved and reset to viewport pixels; it is valid only during the call, so this module never creates or ends one. NativeEditorPainters keeps App's registry, window poll, layer resolver and per-glyph PaintContext maths, and replaces App's transparent overlay widget with two native painters per canvas. Both phases work, so a Reporter background is really drawn under the outlines. When a canvas dies, FontLab drops its native painters itself; the destroyed slot only forgets the Python entry. editor_painters(qt, fontlab, ...) picks this class when the build has the hook, else Glyport's overlay EditorPainters (background as overlay, R054).
